job: Decode individual Markdown chat exports as ordered source occurrences and exact source spans, and inspect or import them through the canonical owner using a configured native MCP client

directive.speaker: agent
directive.quote: Verify the current Markdown export reader against the four named sources: keep every prompt and response occurrence distinct, preserve exact source spans, keep unzoned timestamps as source text, and reuse the existing canonical message owner without publishing private material.

phrasings: Decode individual Markdown chat exports as ordered source occurrences and exact source spans, and inspect or import them through the canonical owner using a configured native MCP client
search.scope: Bounded code-owner search; comprehensive cross-repository capability absence is not claimed. Further owner searches were pending during review.

distinct_from.why: The inspected archive owner reads JSON conversation trees and page-shaped messages; the new format reader supplies that same page shape from Markdown.
The existing message and file importer consumes the new reader; it is not replaced or duplicated.
The native entry reuses this existing configured MCP transport and credential owner rather than implementing either.

The existing tool-run entry receives an admitted file descriptor. The native conversation entry composes the same import owner with an already-configured host MCP bridge and also supports read-only inspection.

preserve: Identity is the ChatGPT /c/<UUID> plus ordered occurrence number.
Every Prompt and Response occurrence remains distinct, including adjacent repeated roles and identical text.
Section-looking headings inside fenced code are message text.
Each occurrence's unzoned local timestamp is retained as source_at and its model separately; at remains null.
UTF-16 source spans, with a header span, reconstruct the decoded Markdown export exactly.
reject: missing title or ChatGPT conversation identity
